title: Globalization of a pointed etale polynomial solution
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ a prime ideal, and $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $E$ be a commutative $R$-algebra with $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\mathfrak q\subset E$ be a prime contracting to the maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR$. Let $n,m\geq0$, let $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in E$ satisfy $f_j(c)=0$ for every $j$, with coefficients evaluated through $A\to R\to E$. There exist a commutative etale $A$-algebra $A'$, an $A$-algebra map $j:A'\to E$, and elements $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in A'$ satisfying $f_j(b)=0$ for every $j$ and $j(b_i)=c_i$ for every $i$. For $\mathfrak p'=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ one has $\mathfrak p'\cap A=\mathfrak p$, and the induced local homomorphism
$$\theta:A'_{\mathfrak p'}\longrightarrow E_{\mathfrak q}$$
is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras carrying $b_i/1$ to $c_i/1$. In particular the induced residue-field isomorphism $\kappa(\mathfrak p')\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ commutes with the structural maps from $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR, lemma-approximation-property-variant, proof after the local approximation: descend the etale algebra, lift the finite solution after principal localization, and identify the local rings.

proof.text: Apply [new-lem-sbc-prime-localization-etale-algebra-model] to the given etale $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra $E$. It gives an etale $A$-algebra $C$, an $A$-algebra map $i:C\to E$, and a multiplicative subset $M\subset C$ making $E$ an $M$-localization of $C$ through $i$. This uses precisely the supplied etaleness; neither Noetherianity nor a G-ring assumption is needed for this globalization.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), proof: globalization paragraph; expanded using algebra.tex Tags 00U2 (10), 00CO, 00CP and 00E3.

proof.text: By the fraction criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], choose $u_i\in C$, $v_i\in M$ with $c_i=i(u_i)i(v_i)^{-1}$. Put $d=\prod_{i=1}^n v_i\in M$, $D=C[1/d]$, and $x_i=u_i(\prod_{k\ne i}v_k)/d\in D$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] gives $i_D:D\to E$ extending $i$, since $i(d)$ is a unit; its formula gives $i_D(x_i)=c_i$. Moreover powers of $d$ lie in $M$, so clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], with the two localizations $C\to D$ and $C\to E$, makes $i_D$ a localization at the image $M_D$ of $M$ in $D$. For $n=0$, take $d=1$ and no $x_i$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), proof: globalization paragraph; expanded using algebra.tex Tags 00U2 (10), 00CO, 00CP and 00E3.

proof.text: Write $e_j=f_j(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in D$. As $i_D$ is an $A$-algebra map, expanding each polynomial as a finite sum of coefficient times monomial gives $i_D(e_j)=f_j(c)=0$. The kernel criterion for the $M_D$-localization from [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] supplies $w_j\in M_D$ with $w_je_j=0$ in $D$. Let $t=\prod_{j=1}^m w_j\in M_D$. For each $j$, $te_j=(\prod_{h\ne j}w_h)(w_je_j)=0$. Set $A'=D[1/t]$ and let $b_i$ be the image of $x_i$. Since $t$ becomes a unit, $f_j(b)=e_j/1=0$. If $m=0$, take $t=1$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), proof: globalization paragraph; expanded using algebra.tex Tags 00U2 (10), 00CO, 00CP and 00E3.

proof.text: Since $i_D(t)$ is a unit, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] extends $i_D$ to an $A$-algebra map $j:A'\to E$, and $j(b_i)=i_D(x_i)=c_i$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], now applied to $D\to D[1/t]$ and the $M_D$-localization $D\to E$, shows that $j$ is a localization at the image $M'$ of $M_D$ in $A'$. Finally apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization] twice: $C$ is etale over $A$, hence $D=C[1/d]$ is etale over $A$, and so is $A'=D[1/t]$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), proof: globalization paragraph; expanded using algebra.tex Tags 00U2 (10), 00CO, 00CP and 00E3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] to the localization $j:A'\to E$ at $M'$ and the specified prime $\mathfrak q\subset E$. It makes $\mathfrak p'=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ prime and gives the canonical isomorphism $\theta:A'_{\mathfrak p'}\to E_{\mathfrak q}$, $a/s\mapsto j(a)/j(s)$, together with its induced residue-field isomorphism. The composite $A\to A'\to E$ is the original structural map, and the contraction of $\mathfrak q$ to $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$; its contraction to $A$ is $\mathfrak p$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and its fraction description. Thus $\mathfrak p'\cap A=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 0CAR (lemma-approximation-property-variant), proof: globalization paragraph; expanded using algebra.tex Tags 00U2 (10), 00CO, 00CP and 00E3.

proof.text: Every $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps outside $\mathfrak p'$ and therefore to a unit of $A'_{\mathfrak p'}$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] gives its $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra structure. Both $R\to E_{\mathfrak q}$ maps, one through $\theta$ and the other through $E$, extend the same map from $A$; uniqueness makes them equal. Hence $\theta$ is an $R$-algebra isomorphism, and its formula gives $\theta(b_i/1)=c_i/1$. Passing to residue fields gives compatible maps from $R$ which kill $\mathfrak pR$, and hence compatible maps from $R/\mathfrak pR=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This proves the final compatibility without choosing an unrelated residue-field isomorphism.
